items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I had met her and knew her, she said, 'Hey, Sonny, I got a job for you all'.

ctx.x: Bricktop was working at Baron Wilkins up at Harlem, very famous Negro nightclub, so -- her name is Ada Bricktop, so I was standing on 7th one day, I had met her and knew her, she said, 'Hey, Sonny, I got a job for you all'. I said, fine. She said 'Baron's down at the basement club.' So we went in Baron's and everything we played was so close together but the other little small bands, they just played hurdy, gurdy, they wasn't together -- they never heard nobody

that played like us. Our six pieces sounded like twelve, and we played so smooth -- we were never loud, very soft, beautiful. We go down there in July and stayed the whole summer and one day, it was a man named Hopper, he produced the colored shows and he was producing a show -- what's the name of it, I stayed there four years. Down at 49th and Broadway, what is the name of that club.
